summary: This is a FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis) data page for the quarterly series GFDEGDQ188S, which measures total U.S. federal public debt as a percentage of GDP, seasonally adjusted. The page shows the latest observation of 121.62069 percent for Q4 2023, last updated March 28, 2024, with quarterly data from 1966-01-01 to 2023-10-01. It also gives the series' construction formula, source attribution, citation details, related series and blog posts, and notes that recessions are shaded on the chart.
one_line: St. Louis Fed FRED page with quarterly U.S. federal total public debt as a percent of GDP, 1966 to Q4 2023.
key_facts: The FRED series GFDEGDQ188S is titled Federal Debt: Total Public Debt as Percent of Gross Domestic Product.
The latest observation shown is Q4 2023 at 121.62069 percent of GDP.
The series was updated March 28, 2024 at 8:07 AM CDT.
The series is quarterly and seasonally adjusted, with units of percent of GDP.
Data covers the period from 1966-01-01 to 2023-10-01.
The first data point, for 1966-01-01, is 40.33999 percent of GDP.
The series value jumped to 132.96365 percent of GDP in 2020-04-01, up from 106.99007 in 2020-01-01.
The series was first constructed by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis in October 2012.
The series is calculated as ((GFDEBTN/1000)/GDP)*100, where GFDEBTN is total public debt in millions of dollars converted to billions.
The underlying data source is the U.S. Office of Management and Budget, and the release is Debt to Gross Domestic Product Ratios.
The suggested citation is dated March 28, 2024 and is retrieved from FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis.
Related series include Federal Surplus or Deficit [-] as Percent of Gross Domestic Product and Gross Federal Debt as Percent of Gross Domestic Product.
Related FRED blog posts include 'Two tales of federal debt', 'Higher public debt, but a lower cost to service it', and 'A lesson in measuring the federal debt'.
The page is tagged Public Domain: Citation Requested.
